lessons.name: A HUNDRED THOUSAND BILLION POEMS: 14 positions, each filled independently by one of 10 interchangeable strips, give 10^14 = 100000000000000 sonnets — the title's number, counted.
lessons.why: A HUNDRED THOUSAND BILLION POEMS: 14 positions, each filled independently by one of 10 interchangeable strips, give 10^14 = 100000000000000 sonnets — the title's number, counted.

lessons.name: WHAT THE BOOK PRINTS AGAINST WHAT IT HOLDS: 10 complete sonnets are printed, and they are 10 of 100000000000000 — one in ten trillion; the other 99999999999990 exist only as choices.
lessons.why: WHAT THE BOOK PRINTS AGAINST WHAT IT HOLDS: 10 complete sonnets are printed, and they are 10 of 100000000000000 — one in ten trillion; the other 99999999999990 exist only as choices.

lessons.name: THE CHOICES MULTIPLY BECAUSE THEY ARE INDEPENDENT: the rhyme sound at a position is shared by all 10 strips, so choosing one position never constrains another, and the count is the product of 14 factors of 10 — the power, written out as the product it is.
lessons.why: THE CHOICES MULTIPLY BECAUSE THEY ARE INDEPENDENT: the rhyme sound at a position is shared by all 10 strips, so choosing one position never constrains another, and the count is the product of 14 factors of 10 — the power, written out as the product it is.

lessons.name: EVERY POEM IS A NUMERAL: which sonnet supplies line i is one decimal digit, so a poem is a 14-digit decimal numeral and the poems are the numerals below 10^14 — the largest poem is 99999999999999, all nines, the last strip at every position.
lessons.why: EVERY POEM IS A NUMERAL: which sonnet supplies line i is one decimal digit, so a poem is a 14-digit decimal numeral and the poems are the numerals below 10^14 — the largest poem is 99999999999999, all nines, the last strip at every position.

lessons.name: THE SONNET'S OWN SHAPE: 14 lines are the octave and the sestet, 8 + 6, so the poems factor as 10^8 · 10^6 — every octave from the book can meet every sestet.
